Her growing league still sends soldiers against the demons, but makes the unfashionable demand that victory should earn every survivor a field, a vote, and permission to lay down a sword.

leaders.angle: The Bannor memory of captivity becomes a public check on the cruelty of their own armies.

Her Witness Houses preserve the Bannor's sacred history alongside these less comfortable records, and their militias have sworn that no commander may burn an archive to protect a reputation.

leaders.name: Matteo Linden
leaders.angle: Pilgrims establish independent hostels on roads where holy orders will only admit their own.
leaders.backstory: Matteo's sister came home from a pilgrimage barefoot after a steward refused their family offerings. He bought a ruined bakehouse and left the door open to the first stranger who reached it. There are now lay houses in six provinces, each with a table long enough to seat both pilgrims and the people they are fleeing.

leaders.name: Imena Wakefold
leaders.angle: One sanctuary keeps a sealed burial hill free of both relic hunters and official custodians.
leaders.backstory: Imena cleared a ruined chapterhouse and found that the dirt beneath its floor whispered living people's names. Her order marked the site on no maps and used the stones to build an ordinary sheepfold. It now shelters families whose ancestors would be instruments in somebody else's hands if the fold's true boundary became known.

leaders.name: Levan Pledge
leaders.angle: A keeper of holy hospitality converts guests' gratitude into debts they can never repay.
leaders.backstory: Levan started collecting vows of thanks while the refugees in his care still had no money. He kept each on a reed slip and redeemed small promises first, for a morning's labor or a winter blanket. The bundle has grown hefty enough that he can decide who marries, who travels, and which children will keep the sanctuary books.

leaders.name: Enna Bramblehook
leaders.angle: A city's gardeners gain authority by keeping famine at bay through practical seed craft.
leaders.backstory: Enna watched the gardens inside a siege ring go to seed as most of the remaining land was requisitioned for troops. She grafted bitter roots onto fruiting plants, then sent the cuttings to households too poor to buy seed. When the walls reopened, local families kept exchanging plants through her long after the old ration masters had run out of work.

leaders.name: Serediel
leaders.angle: A rebel angel interprets the war against demons as a duty to protect the living who are caught in it.
leaders.backstory: Serediel once held a passage into Hell open while Basium's warriors pursued a retreating demon host. Mortals fleeing in the other direction forced her to choose between closing the trap and keeping their escape route clear. She stayed until the last child crossed, and now leads angels and mortal auxiliaries who measure a battle by the people brought safely home as well as the demons destroyed.

leaders.angle: The rebel host needs roads, workshops, and mortal supply agreements as urgently as another glorious charge.
leaders.backstory: Othra counted the hammers, sandals, and grain sacks abandoned after a Mercurian victory and realized that the next campaign would starve its mortal allies. She established repair yards along the host's route, buying supplies through fixed agreements instead of letting victorious angels requisition whatever they pleased. Her garrison towns are now indispensable to the crusade, but she will withhold a bridge or a wagon train from any commander who refuses to honor the price.

leaders.angle: An anti-demon Mercurian splinter mistakes uncompromising purpose for righteousness and enslaves the people it claims to defend.

He decided that mortal hesitation had prolonged the war, and began binding rescued settlements to compulsory service until the last demon in existence was dead. His followers still fight the Infernals with terrible courage, but execute deserters and take children as guarantees of obedience, making a prison of the liberation they proclaim.

leaders.angle: The immortal host must preserve the particular lives of the dead instead of treating every returning soul as another soldier.

She gathered their remaining memories into laments, then sent mortal singers to carry those songs back to the villages that still waited for news. Angels who fear becoming nothing but weapons gather around her memorial courts, where a soul is given time to remember its name before anyone offers it a sword.

He began building layered wards that smothered hostile magic and insisted that friendly summoners leave their workings outside the same boundary. The mortal enclaves beneath his pale barriers pay for his protection and live under his severe restrictions, while Mercurian captains argue over whether the sanctuaries preserve their cause or obstruct it.

leaders.angle: An angel returns the belongings of the dead and gives their families a voice in the celestial host.
leaders.backstory: Aureth's first body still carried a wooden badge carved by the soldier's daughter. He tracked down the family and found a line of others asking the host for possessions no officer had thought to collect. His companies now return one keepsake for every body they borrow and ask the survivors to name the next city they defend.

leaders.name: Meriel Bronze Dawn
leaders.angle: An angelic works corps claims the right to govern the towns it rebuilds.
leaders.backstory: Meriel watched the first winged regiment crush a water tower when its soldiers landed in an unfamiliar square. She devised stepped stone platforms that could take the weight and leave the wells accessible. The engineers who build them remain after the troops march, arguing that a garrison is no better than its stairs.

leaders.name: Caradriel Pale Fire
leaders.angle: An angel presses an unyielding war of prevention against any city judged capable of harboring demons.
leaders.backstory: Caradriel's company took an unguarded gate and lost half its borrowed bodies to a demon sheltering in a grain store. She brought the grain scale back to camp and made it the emblem of a tribunal that could seize supplies on suspicion alone. Her towns now run on confiscated grain and pray each morning to remain above suspicion.

leaders.name: Sorad Veiled Seal
leaders.angle: Host archivists demand proof before assigning the resurrected to an earthly family.
leaders.backstory: Sorad watched two villages claim the same angel after each lost a son at a disputed crossing. He established a waiting house for such cases and began recording what the angels could recall before they heard anybody's testimony. The house answers to him today because too many officers want its ledgers to endorse a convenient ancestry.

leaders.angle: Human and angel soldiers share command in a coalition formerly divided by rank.
leaders.backstory: Avona carried messages between the city guard and an angelic unit whose commanders refused to share a table. She had two small benches built into the chasm wall so they could confer while both sides watched. By the second siege the benches wore smooth, and the troops called for Avona when their commanders disagreed.

leaders.name: Mavra Wickhand
leaders.angle: An itinerant toy-maker preserves ordinary Luchuirp lives rather than restoring an empire or accumulating a treasury.
leaders.backstory: Mavra began repairing nursery toys in a refugee quarter where no family could afford a new golem. She fitted broken household constructs with little theaters that replayed the songs and trades of villages lost beneath the ice, carefully distinguishing their stored performances from living minds. Her traveling workshops became the meeting places of scattered clans, and their patrons asked her to arbitrate disputes that the city guilds ignored. She now leads a league of small makers whose first demand is that the poor inherit more of their ancestors than their debts.

leaders.name: Odrik Sluice
leaders.angle: Agricultural infrastructure and the political power of maintenance crews, rather than celebrated masterworks.
leaders.backstory: Odrik inherited a canal district whose magnificent ancient pumps had stopped because nobody remembered how to service them. He replaced their ingenious but irreplaceable mechanisms with plain golems that any village mason could mend. Farmers rewarded him with authority over their water schedules, and his maintenance crews gradually became a government crossing several guild jurisdictions. He will sell grain to either side of a war, but closes the sluices of anyone who tries to make his crews into soldiers.

leaders.name: Kelna Brasshear
leaders.angle: The ethics and safety of enchantment, without assuming every golem has Barnaxus's exceptional personhood.
leaders.backstory: Kelna learned to diagnose failing enchantments by listening to the uneven hum inside a golem's chest. After a workshop accident, she discovered that a celebrated master had concealed a spirit-binding inside an otherwise ordinary laborer's frame. She insisted that the bound being be released and that every workshop publish what its animating spells actually contained. Apprentices and cautious householders have since formed a faction around her demand that mastery include responsibility for what answers when a maker gives an order.

leaders.backstory: Vorra rescued several indebted workshops by buying their golems and leasing the same servants back to them. Each repair introduced another proprietary enchantment, until an entire district could neither harvest nor build without her permission. When its council challenged her fees, she recalled every leased construct on the morning the flood defenses needed reinforcement. The council submitted, and her creditor cities now call submission to her contracts the price of civilization.

leaders.angle: A survivor's insistence on shelters and manual safeguards challenges the civilization's dependence on enchantment.
leaders.backstory: Durn was a shelter mason when a hostile dispelling left his settlement's enchanted doors open during a raid. He saved its children through an unfinished service tunnel and spent the following winter designing gates that living hands could close. His fortified workshops still employ golems, but every essential system has an unenchanted second means of operation. Border towns follow him because he promises neither perfect machines nor another retreat beneath the world, only the chance to survive when a marvel fails.

Her registries gave lamia households, centaur companies, and human guilds enforceable places in the same administration. Those categories also hardened into rules about which peoples could hold which offices, a restriction she defends as the necessary scaffolding of peace. The officials who support her want the confederacy to survive an absent king, even if its citizens must fit more neatly into her ledgers.

leaders.angle: A centaur frontier commander gives the outlying settlements a political voice independent of the great cities.

When an evacuation order abandoned three allied villages, he held the road until their people could follow. He remains loyal to the confederacy, but insists that citizenship include the right to influence decisions made behind distant city walls.

leaders.angle: An urban harpy faction brings the city above street level into politics, mixing civic culture with extralegal resistance.
leaders.backstory: Ilyra organized the harpy messengers who nested above a city that taxed their deliveries but refused to recognize their homes. A landlord's attempt to tear down the high quarter became a week of vanished rent chests and mocking songs delivered through every upper window. Her couriers now protect rooftop markets, smuggle dissidents between districts, and maintain the fastest warning network in the confederacy. She bargains with the city below as its indispensable neighbor, never as its obedient ornament.

leaders.angle: An authoritarian merchant preserves the multiracial metropolis while making its promise of asylum a source of exploitation.
leaders.backstory: Avar rose by supplying food and housing to newcomers whom the royal administration had welcomed faster than it could accommodate. He converted those emergency advances into hereditary obligations, then purchased offices that let him decide when a family had repaid them. His city admits almost anyone and displays every people of Erebus in its splendid public processions. Behind that hospitality, his magistrates make leaving one's assigned work far harder than entering the gates.

leaders.name: Meren Glasshand
leaders.angle: A civic skeptic questions rule by personal supernatural charisma without abandoning the confederacy's pluralism.
leaders.backstory: Meren investigated a neighborhood magistrate who had used a charm to turn public consultations into unanimous acclaim. Exposure earned her a shattered hand and a new following among citizens uneasy about the court's almost religious reverence for its boy-king. Her assemblies require testimony outside magical influence and publish dissent beside the winning decision. She asks whether a people held together by one extraordinary ruler can learn to trust its ordinary disagreements.
leaders.portrait: Middle-aged human woman with light-brown skin, angular face, short silver-streaked black hair and thoughtful dark eyes. Asymmetrical charcoal advocate's coat with mint-green lining. Her articulated translucent glass left hand pulls a red censor's ribbon off an open public record while her living hand spreads its pages; bright public assembly hall with diverse blurred silhouettes, cool defiant scrutiny.
leaders.primary_palette: Charcoal gray with mint green accents
leaders.hand_activity: Pulling a censor's ribbon off an open public record with her articulated glass hand while spreading the pages with her living hand.
leaders.clothing: An asymmetrical charcoal advocate's coat with mint-green lining, plain linen shirt and an exposed articulated glass left hand.

leaders.name: Philia Copperroof
leaders.angle: Winged laborers claim public air routes through the towers they keep standing.
leaders.backstory: Philia spent her first wages replacing a scaffold that humans could not reach and her fellow harpies were forbidden to land on. She kept the invoices and drew the first survey of all the roofs a city could not maintain without them. The workers now run the rooftop stations and keep a lane open even to people who cannot afford to fly.
leaders.portrait: Copper-brown female harpy with dark curls, ochre shoulder feathers and one gold eye, roof bridges and a high windy city
leaders.primary_palette: Peacock teal vest, copper feathers and blue sky
leaders.hand_activity: Pulls a bright chalk line between two rooftop pegs
leaders.clothing: Peacock teal harness vest with copper toggles and open shoulder seams

leaders.name: Rython Twelvearches
leaders.epithet: First Speaker of the Covered Market
leaders.angle: Stallholders make their market an independent town built to fit every kind of body.
leaders.backstory: A centaur's hooves once cracked the stairs to the market and Rython was charged for the damage although he was standing outside. He bought a sunken quarry and filled it with gentle ramps, high stalls and aisles wide enough for three bodies like his. He charges to cover the paving and lets even the people who sneered at it come in out of the rain.
leaders.portrait: Male centaur with a wide tan face, cropped grizzled beard and chestnut horse body partly suggested below frame, vast curved market ramp
leaders.primary_palette: Persimmon orange waistcoat, gray stone and chestnut leather
leaders.hand_activity: Slides a stamped weight along a balance beam
leaders.clothing: Persimmon waistcoat and soft gray shoulder wrap with coin loops

leaders.name: Isil Coilbank
leaders.angle: A deed broker coerces families whose homes stand on land built up by several peoples at once.
leaders.backstory: Isil amassed deeds to the old riverbed while its lamia houses were still built on floats. When the river shifted inland, she charged the residents for the reclaimed foundations under their homes and took their boats as collateral. Her tenants are free to move, provided they leave their furnishings and a child who knows the ledger.
leaders.portrait: Female lamia with tawny skin, black waves of hair, silver-green scales and hint of serpent coils, covered canal quay
leaders.primary_palette: Imperial purple gown, oxidized silver and dark green scales
leaders.hand_activity: Threads a ring of iron boat keys onto a split silver hoop
leaders.clothing: Purple banker gown with a deep scalloped collar and silver wrist bands

leaders.name: Tevin Manywindows
leaders.angle: A mixed neighborhood writes civic law from the practical business of sharing buildings.
leaders.backstory: Tevin inherited a boarding house whose forebears had added a door for each new kind of lodger. He took the doors out of the price of rooms and set up the first tenants' festival with the proceeds from the old hinges. Visitors still take the number of doors for a sign of disorder until they see who carries whom out in a fire.
leaders.portrait: Young adult dark-skinned human man with a thin goatee, lively eyes and a shock of black hair, round-headed doors in a colorful courtyard
leaders.primary_palette: Marigold vest, turquoise doors and cedar-brown beams
leaders.hand_activity: Seats a spare brass hinge onto a little wooden door frame
leaders.clothing: Marigold embroidered host's vest with broad turquoise lapels

leaders.name: Asen Curtainfall
leaders.angle: Outer settlements insist their right to exist cannot depend on a city's decision to extend its walls.
leaders.backstory: Asen grew up in a settlement that vanished each time the capital commissioned a new map. She sewed her street onto the edge of the maps and offered the rest of the bolt to other villages missing from the survey. The patchwork hangs in her court because it takes a succession of people to carry it anywhere else.
leaders.portrait: Older pale human woman with a black-silver braid and one eyebrow scar, embroidered map above a low settlement wall
leaders.primary_palette: Raspberry mantle, chalk linen and storm-gray ground
leaders.hand_activity: Stitches a corner of rough linen onto a large cloth plan
leaders.clothing: Raspberry wool mantle over a long chalk-gray tunic and capped sleeves

leaders.name: Saeril Reedkeeper
leaders.angle: The material economy of a forest civilization: seed reserves, seasonal obligations, and the leverage of food.
leaders.backstory: Saeril kept the seed exchanges between groves whose nobles considered accounting beneath an elf's dignity. When blight destroyed an autumn harvest, his unglamorous reserves fed households that the court's songs had not remembered to count. The groves accepted his common calendar of planting, loans, and repayment, giving their steward influence that neither birth nor magic had earned him. He now trades that influence for secure borders and favorable treaties, regarding a glorious war as a particularly wasteful kind of famine.
leaders.portrait: Mature male Ljosalfar elf with amber-brown skin, long pointed ears, narrow lined face and dark hair threaded with gray. Moss-green sleeveless steward's surcoat over buff-gold linen, reed-woven shoulder guards. He pours seeds from a small basket into a calibrated wooden measure and checks their level with his free hand; living granary trees and hanging baskets, dry patient competence under filtered sun.
leaders.primary_palette: Moss green with buff gold accents
leaders.hand_activity: Pouring seeds from a small reed basket into a calibrated wooden measure, checking the level with his free hand.
leaders.clothing: A moss-green sleeveless steward's surcoat over buff-gold linen, reed-woven shoulder guards and plain tied cuffs.

leaders.name: Nethra Cinderbough
leaders.angle: Reconstruction and skilled adaptation after forest destruction, rather than vengeance or royal ritual.
leaders.backstory: Nethra returned from border service to find that a magical fire had spared her village's roots and destroyed nearly everything above them. She persuaded its survivors to build around the scarred trunks instead of abandoning them or demanding impossible restoration. Her bridges, cisterns, and sheltered nurseries made the damaged grove habitable while new growth slowly returned. Other burned communities now seek her leadership, and she measures victory by how many people can come home after the soldiers leave.
leaders.portrait: Adult Ljosalfar elf woman, copper skin, long pointed ears, close-cropped auburn hair and pale healed burn scar across one cheek. Copper-rust leather work vest with dark-pine sleeves and a carpenter's belt. Both hands draw a small drawknife along a young bridge branch, shaping it carefully at chest height; blackened living trunks carrying new canopy bridges, hopeful green daylight and resilient practical concentration.
leaders.primary_palette: Copper rust with dark pine accents
leaders.hand_activity: Shaping a young bridge branch with a small drawknife, both hands pulling the blade carefully toward her.
leaders.clothing: A copper-rust leather work vest with dark-pine sleeves, reinforced shoulder straps and a broad carpenter's belt.

leaders.name: Iovain Stillroot
leaders.angle: A cruel Seelie ecological absolutism, distinct from the Svartalfar court's intrigue and predation.
leaders.backstory: Iovain tended a sacred grove through decades of rebuilding and came to regard every cleared field as another wound in the world's recovery. He began planting boundary trees across neighboring farms, preaching that the forest's return outweighed the claims of short-lived peoples. When hungry refugees cut those saplings for firewood, his followers drove them out and consecrated their abandoned houses as shrines. He offers the Ljosalfar an endless summer purchased by treating everyone beyond its shade as expendable.
leaders.portrait: Ancient male Ljosalfar elf, gaunt pale-gold face, very long pointed ears, white hair braided with ivy. Flowing bone-ivory priestly robes and angular citron-yellow leaf collar. One hand presses living roots down into a cracked boundary stone while the other makes a deliberate blessing over the growth; dense summer foliage swallowing a ruined lintel, serene ruthless conviction in beautiful warm light.
leaders.primary_palette: Bone ivory with citron yellow accents
leaders.hand_activity: Pressing living roots into the cracked top of an old boundary stone, one hand forcing them downward while the other blesses the growth.
leaders.clothing: Flowing bone-ivory priestly robes, angular citron-yellow leaf collar and a tall narrow crown of woven ivy.

leaders.name: Aelwen Many-Vows
leaders.angle: Elven longevity becomes an obligation to remember mortal allies rather than grounds for indifference to them.
leaders.backstory: Aelwen was sent to renew a treaty and discovered that three generations of its human signatories had died while her court delayed an answer. She stayed to record their names and found that their descendants remembered elven silence more clearly than elven promises. Her traveling witnesses now carry the histories of mortal allies between groves, insisting that an oath cannot wait upon the convenience of the long-lived. Border households and younger elves have made her the voice of those who must share a world before they can afford to understand it.
leaders.portrait: Young-looking mature Ljosalfar elf woman, deep-brown skin, long pointed ears, dark curls in a low knot and expressive thoughtful eyes. Cerulean traveling cloak with coral-pink treaty ribbons, softly pleated linen collar. She presses an inked thumb beside old human handprints on a treaty while steadying the parchment with her other hand; forest embassy porch and empty human-sized chair, earnest openhearted attention.
leaders.primary_palette: Cerulean blue with coral pink accents
leaders.hand_activity: Pressing an inked thumb beside several old handprints on a treaty, steadying the parchment with her other hand.
leaders.clothing: A cerulean traveling cloak with coral-pink treaty ribbons, softly pleated linen collar and a weathered cross-body book satchel.

leaders.name: Namar Oathmolt
leaders.angle: A counter-enchanter protects the forest from benevolent and hostile magic alike, limiting even his own court's mages.
leaders.backstory: Namar once strengthened the spells that encouraged a frontier grove to grow, until competing enchantments left its trees flowering and dying in the same week. Undoing the damage taught him to prize limits more than displays of power. His wardens now inspect foreign relics, royal experiments, and druidic blessings with the same suspicion, earning enemies among allies who believe good intentions should exempt them. Groves tired of becoming somebody else's magical answer support his austere promise that their seasons will remain their own.
leaders.portrait: Middle-aged male Ljosalfar elf, angular olive face, long pointed ears, black hair in a severe short tail and one milky damaged eye. Fitted aubergine coat with cool-gray protective gauntlets and minimal silver ward seams. He lifts one crystal shard from a wooden containment hoop with long tongs while adjusting the ward clasp with his other hand; forest boundary stones, faint restrained blue ward light, austere vigilant concentration.
leaders.primary_palette: Aubergine purple with cool gray accents
leaders.hand_activity: Lifting one dangerous crystal shard out of a containment hoop with long tongs while adjusting the hoop's ward clasp with his other hand.
leaders.clothing: A fitted aubergine counter-enchanter's coat with cool-gray protective gauntlets, close collar and minimal silver ward seams.

leaders.name: Calen Birdbranch
leaders.epithet: The Messenger of the Lower Boughs
leaders.angle: Young settlements claim a voice through a relay that runs below the old canopy roads.
leaders.backstory: Calen tended messenger birds that were trained to fly only to the manors in their breeding book. He let a clutch nest in a roadside willow and raised the fledglings to land where woodcutters offered a perch. The lord of the high branches still receives the news, a little later than the bark peelers.
leaders.portrait: Young adult golden-brown male forest elf with pointed ears and close brown curls, perched in a network of branches
leaders.primary_palette: Golden yellow tunic, lilac dusk and copper bark
leaders.hand_activity: Coaxes a small speckled bird onto a gloved wrist
leaders.clothing: Golden feather-trimmed sleeve and violet travel vest

leaders.name: Mevara Rainsuture
leaders.angle: Tree surgeons organize remote groves around the living crossings they maintain.
leaders.backstory: When a flood took her bridge, Mevara followed its torn limbs downstream and transplanted the living ends. They took root on opposite banks within sight of an old ferry that had charged an armful of firewood to carry a child. Crossing dues in her new groves consist of watering a branch on the way past.
leaders.portrait: Middle-aged dark-skinned female forest elf, silver-tipped dreads and long ears, living root bridge across a flooded valley
leaders.primary_palette: Vermilion rain cape, moss and pearl-gray light
leaders.hand_activity: Knots a strip of cloth around two living branches to train them
leaders.clothing: Vermilion rain cape with fitted moss-green forearm wraps

leaders.name: Thalan Ambervow
leaders.angle: A traditionalist appropriates woodland by giving ancient trees rights only his court can hear.
leaders.backstory: Thalan was a witness when the oldest pine of his province fell across a boundary ditch. In the resin he claimed to read a deed covering both banks, then the houses and fields adjoining them. He invites any dispossessed farmer to attend the hearings, provided they can offer testimony in a language the court accepts from trees.
leaders.portrait: Gaunt pale male elf with a long chestnut beard and blade-sharp ears, towering ancient pines and a resin altar
leaders.primary_palette: Wine violet robe, amber resin and forest black
leaders.hand_activity: Tilts an amber resin shard to the light above a shallow stone dish
leaders.clothing: Wine-violet priestly coat with split sleeves and a black shoulder collar

leaders.name: Finnel Woodmeter
leaders.angle: A licensed woodcutter earns protection for trees and wages for the people who harvest them.
leaders.backstory: Finnel never felled a trunk he could return to in seven years and cut again. He taught the villages to count regrowth alongside their timber before the merchants could lay claim to it. His contracts infuriate the court because coppices are now worth enough that a worker can take a lord to court for stealing one.
leaders.portrait: Stocky tawny male elf with pointed ears, curly cropped black hair and hawkish eyes, evenly coppiced riverside grove
leaders.primary_palette: Sky blue work coat, toasted bark and wheat
leaders.hand_activity: Checks the girth of a sapling with a loop of measuring tape
leaders.clothing: Sky-blue canvas with a broad pale shoulder pad and dark gloves

leaders.name: Lethiel Hollowtone
leaders.angle: A researcher gives every grove access to warnings once reserved for the oldest families.
leaders.backstory: Lethiel suspected the humming that preceded a blight came from ordinary roots rather than a family spirit. She sank hollow tubes at each farm and invited the youngest worker to tell her the note before the family elders could interpret it. A ring of groves now reports to her when the note changes, sometimes in time to cut a branch and save a valley.
leaders.portrait: Copper-skinned female elf in her fifties, angled gray bob, long ears and strong cheekbones, woodland listening well
leaders.primary_palette: Ivory robe, cypress shadows and pink quartz
leaders.hand_activity: Lowers a hollow rosewood pipe into a root cavity
leaders.clothing: Ivory listening mantle with a fanned leaf-like collar and rose cuffs

leaders.name: Brunna Chalkvein
leaders.angle: Dwarven caution serves public refuge and disaster preparation, rather than royal authority or mercantile expansion.
leaders.backstory: Brunna commanded a mine rescue when a spring thaw flooded workings that three feuding clans each claimed were another's responsibility. She cut through a private vault wall to reach the trapped crews, then submitted herself to the compensation court beside the people she had saved. The settlement established a common emergency fund and gave its administration to her. Her shelter towns admit outsiders during disasters under strict inventories and shared duties, making measured trust a matter of engineering rather than sentiment.
leaders.portrait: Older Khazad dwarf woman with ruddy-brown skin, broad strong face, close gray braids and chalk across her cheek. Vermilion rescue captain's coat with cream shoulder markings and broad leather braces. She actively swings a bronze alarm bell with one hand while directing an evacuation with a decisive open-palmed sweep of the other; reinforced stone floodgate shelter, warm lamplight, commanding reassuring urgency.
leaders.primary_palette: Vermilion red with cream accents
leaders.hand_activity: Swinging a bronze alarm bell outward with one hand while directing an evacuation with a decisive open-palmed sweep of the other.
leaders.clothing: A vermilion rescue captain's coat with cream shoulder markings, broad leather braces and a reinforced miner's collar.

leaders.name: Dorrik Ledgergrave
leaders.angle: A Khazad moral philosopher twists the vault's promise of security into a doctrine that prices people by their assets.
leaders.backstory: Dorrik began as an arbitrator asked to decide how much a collapsed mine owed its dead workers' families. His tables of compensation became a general theory that a person's claim to protection should equal the wealth they preserved for the hold. Rich clans endowed his school, while debtors found that even an honest accident could reduce their descendants' standing. His creditor faction keeps full vaults and orderly streets by making poverty evidence that a dwarf deserves less of both.
leaders.portrait: Elderly Khazad dwarf man, pale sallow skin, precisely squared black-and-silver beard and small cold eyes behind round lenses. Midnight-blue academic robe with rigid old-gold yoke and square sleeves. He sets a tiny worker figurine on one pan of a balance while adding gold weights to the other, studying it with grave pitiless calculation; geometrically ordered vault alcove, low amber light.
leaders.primary_palette: Midnight blue with old gold accents
leaders.hand_activity: Placing a tiny worker figurine on one pan of a balance while adding gold weights to the other, scrutinizing the result.
leaders.clothing: A midnight-blue academic robe with rigid old-gold yoke, square sleeves and a precise gold counting chain.

leaders.name: Helvi Handseer
leaders.angle: The runewarden tradition and contested ancestral memory, including the histories prestigious clans would erase.
leaders.backstory: Helvi lost her sight after years reading the ancestral pillars by candlelight and learned the old runewardens' art of knowing a history by touch. While restoring a damaged hall, she found that the names of banished kin had been chiseled away beneath an approved account of their disgrace. She carved those names into a new pillar without pretending their owners had been innocent. Smaller clans now gather behind her demand that the Khazad preserve the whole record, even when remembrance threatens a useful peace between powerful families.
leaders.portrait: Elderly blind Khazad dwarf woman with medium-brown skin, cloudy eyes, deep patient lines and long silver hair over one shoulder. Pale-lavender wrap robe with earth-ocher stone-carver's apron and soft plain cuffs. She chisels a fresh rune into a stone tablet with one hand while tracing the preceding carved line with the fingertips of the other; candlelit ancestral pillars, solemn tactile patience, no glowing eyes.
leaders.primary_palette: Pale lavender with earth ocher accents
leaders.hand_activity: Chiseling a rune into a stone tablet while tracing the preceding carved line with the fingertips of her other hand.
leaders.clothing: A pale-lavender runewarden's wrap robe with earth-ocher apron, soft unadorned cuffs and a hood folded behind the shoulders.

leaders.name: Ordan Outledge
leaders.angle: Landless dwarves and mobile prospecting companies challenge the assumption that security begins with an established hold.
leaders.backstory: Ordan's family returned from prospecting to discover that their clan had sold its marginal homes to settle a larger house's debt. He gathered other dispossessed crews into a caravan that opened abandoned passes and lived from salvage, surveys, and armed escort. When neighboring lords imposed tolls, his companies seized the tollhouses and offered the same roads to everyone who paid for their upkeep. He seeks enough land to found a hold, but his followers fear that becoming respectable will mean shutting the gates on people like themselves.
leaders.portrait: Young adult Khazad dwarf man, weathered tan skin, windburned cheeks, unruly dark-red beard braided with iron tags. Leather-umber sleeveless trail coat over crimson wool and a battered steel shoulder plate. He sets a survey compass on a folded mountain map and scratches in a new pass route with a short iron point; exposed high mountain pass and caravan bells, restless scrappy confidence.
leaders.primary_palette: Leather umber with crimson accents
leaders.hand_activity: Setting a survey compass on a mountain map and scratching a new pass route into it with a short iron point.
leaders.clothing: A leather-umber sleeveless trail coat over crimson wool, battered steel shoulder plate and a collection of iron survey tags.

leaders.name: Sovna Trueweight
leaders.angle: The historical trauma of magical fraud produces transparent standards for outsiders, rather than isolation or retaliatory cheating.
leaders.backstory: Sovna trained as an assayer in a hold where an illusory shipment had ruined three generations of one family. Instead of forbidding foreign trade, she built testing rooms where dwarf and stranger could watch the same metal weighed, scratched, and checked against enchantment. Her publicly recorded standards attracted merchants excluded by clan monopolies and gave honest small traders a way to challenge richer rivals. The market towns have chosen her to lead them because she treats distrust as a problem to solve before a bargain, rather than a debt to collect afterward.
leaders.portrait: Middle-aged Khazad dwarf woman, dark-brown skin, broad freckled nose, practical black crown braid and alert friendly eyes. Emerald-green guild waistcoat over clean white rolled sleeves and a narrow assay apron. She rubs a coin across a black touchstone and points to the fresh metal streak with her other hand for a customer; open daylight testing booth, modest coin trays, candid meticulous assurance.
leaders.primary_palette: Emerald green with clean white accents
leaders.hand_activity: Rubbing a coin across a black touchstone while pointing to its fresh metal streak with her other hand for an unseen customer.
leaders.clothing: An emerald-green guild waistcoat over clean white rolled sleeves, narrow leather assay apron and plain brass badge.

leaders.name: Berga Ironwedge
leaders.epithet: First Hand of the Rescue Crew
leaders.angle: A rescue brotherhood makes unsafe holds answer to the people who shore them up.
leaders.backstory: Berga's crew came to a collapsed adit with orders to save the ore chests before the men. She wedged the chests under a crack and hauled out enough witnesses to overturn the order in court. The holds that ignored the judgment still keep their pit bosses, but each deep crew carries a copy of her rescue charter.
leaders.portrait: Deep brown dwarf woman with massive shoulders, gray wire curls and full cheeks, braced mine chamber with gold seams
leaders.primary_palette: Safety orange coat, basalt and pale oak wedges
leaders.hand_activity: Taps a pale wooden wedge into a timber prop
leaders.clothing: Orange pit jacket with a soot-gray fur yoke and broad leather wrists

leaders.name: Orik Cinderhall
leaders.epithet: The Last Voice at the Smelter
leaders.angle: Smelter crews pool warmth, housing and credit away from the gold vaults.
leaders.backstory: Orik wanted to know why his apprentices froze upstairs while his slag boiled beneath their feet. He rerouted the waste heat through a row of affordable apartments before the hold's surveyors found out. The families bought the next furnace themselves and sent him to bargain for the mountain's water.
leaders.portrait: Dark tan stocky male dwarf, long black sideburns and a square goatee, brick smelter with furnace pipes
leaders.primary_palette: Prussian blue coat, flame orange and smoky gray
leaders.hand_activity: Twists a heavy stopcock on a copper heating pipe
leaders.clothing: Prussian blue thermal smelter coat with slate metal shoulder rivets

leaders.name: Huldra Sevenvault
leaders.angle: The owners of sealed vaults collect rents even from holds unable to reach their own deposits.
leaders.backstory: Huldra bought a vault that had been locked since an earthquake and leased the idea of the gold within it to desperate holds. She offered to forgive any hold that opened the vault, so long as it signed over its rights to the gold if it failed. Now that seven tunnels have collapsed in the attempt, her creditors prefer to keep paying and let the door remain a matter of faith.
leaders.portrait: Pale older dwarf woman with black lacquered braids and fine wrinkles, towering unmarked vault door with dark stonework
leaders.primary_palette: Mulberry velvet, polished steel and vellum beige
leaders.hand_activity: Turns a heavy vault combination wheel one notch
leaders.clothing: Mulberry velvet factor's gown with a lacquer-black square collar

leaders.name: Garum Veinwalker
leaders.angle: Surface Khazad establish ports and trading farms with the same rights as underground holds.
leaders.backstory: Garum returned from shipping season with grain, new words and a wife who had never seen a vault. The keepers assigned them a cellar outside the gates, so he made it a warehouse and invited the coast hands to live nearby. The first surface consul was elected in that cellar with the shutters open.
leaders.portrait: Burly copper-skinned dwarf man in his forties, short sandy beard and windburned cheeks, terraced coastal warehouses
leaders.primary_palette: Jade green waistcoat, cream canvas and bronze light
leaders.hand_activity: Hauls a cloth grain sack onto a wooden counting ledge
leaders.clothing: Jade merchant's waistcoat with rolled cream sailors' sleeves

leaders.name: Ursi Mothsilver
leaders.angle: A silverworker discovers why older galleries are empty and makes their lost work available to independent holds.
leaders.backstory: Ursi followed a tarnished thread into a shaft where all the assay marks had been chiseled away. She strung salvaged silver together by the sequence of tool marks and found a generation of makers the vault families never recorded. Neighboring holds send her strips of their own silver to see whose work she can name.
leaders.portrait: Elderly dark dwarf woman with shaven temples, thick snow-white braid and clever eyes, narrow galleries with glittering flecks
leaders.primary_palette: Ice mint wool, white silver and plum shadows
leaders.hand_activity: Feeds a ribbon of etched silver through a handheld loupe
leaders.clothing: Mint wool smock with wide violet silk sleeves and a curved silver clasp

leaders.name: Velisar
leaders.angle: An immortal witness who spends the Sidar's accumulated memory on justice outside their borders.
leaders.backstory: Velisar became a shade to remember the names of a village that a victorious king ordered struck from every chronicle. Centuries later, she discovered that she could recall its tax rolls perfectly but no longer remember her sister's laugh. She now leads a company of witnesses who record testimony before fading can empty it of feeling, and brings their records into foreign courts even when Sandalphon's seclusion would be safer.

leaders.name: Nemeia
leaders.angle: Patient commerce and contractual memory instead of isolation or military guardianship.
leaders.backstory: Nemeia was a mortal factor hired to settle debts whose Sidar creditors had forgotten why they were owed. She learned to translate a shade's century-long patience into leases, warehouses and quiet purchases along the roads beyond the mist. Her trading houses now provision several hidden cities, and the shades accept her leadership because she alone can tell them which obligations still belong to the living.

leaders.hand_activity: Threading two strands of a knotted credit cord through a brass reckoning ring with both hands
leaders.clothing: Plum merchant wrap with a high folded shoulder and close-fitting brass-trimmed sleeves

leaders.name: Orven
leaders.angle: The living inhabitants of Sidar cities claim a political voice while retaining their immortal neighbors.
leaders.backstory: Orven kept the ferry to a hidden Sidar city long after its immortal council stopped noticing the villages on the opposite bank. When a flood drove those villagers to his landing, he opened the passage and housed them in districts that had stood empty for generations. The mortal households made him their speaker, and he persuades the Grey that a city can shelter new lives without surrendering the old ones it preserves.

leaders.hand_activity: Turning the iron crank of a ferry winch while reaching out to steady an arriving passenger

leaders.name: Satha
leaders.angle: The wish to preserve a hidden city hardens into the coercive preservation of its inhabitants.
leaders.backstory: Satha once painted portraits so that newly faded shades could remember the faces they had surrendered. After raiders burned her gallery, she enclosed her district behind wards that admitted neither fire nor uninvited travelers. Her followers call it the safest place in Erebus, but she now forbids residents to leave and treats every change of loyalty, trade or family as damage to a collection entrusted to her care.

leaders.name: Terev
leaders.angle: A restless artisan sends Sidar retrieval expeditions into the world rather than waiting within it.
leaders.backstory: Terev chose fading so that death could never interrupt the mosaic he had spent half his life assembling. He returned from seclusion to find its missing panels displayed as trophies in the halls of three foreign dynasties. His fellow dispossessed artisans furnish a small army that steals their works back, while his refusal to ask who now treasures those works keeps restitution perilously close to conquest.

leaders.name: Naresh Lintelmist
leaders.angle: A border porter negotiates daylight passage for shades and their mortal relations alike.
leaders.backstory: Naresh kept a toll station where travellers could shelter from the hour the shades were most visible. He repaired the shutters after every raid, leaving one unlatched for people who could no longer grasp the handle. Ordinary travellers now leave their names at the station beside the shades they still recognize.

leaders.name: Maelis Frostlinen
leaders.epithet: The Weaver of the Missing Years
leaders.angle: Retired shades piece together the years they no longer remember without selling them to collectors.
leaders.backstory: Maelis began weaving dates into the strips she used to bind her winter clothes. Other shades brought her a loose end here and there, most of them as eager to forget it as to have it recorded. Her workshop keeps the resulting cloth folded so a visitor can ask for just the year she wants to see.

leaders.name: Soren of the Span
leaders.angle: A crossing broker charges shades memories when service no longer has another cost.
leaders.backstory: Soren built a bridge broad enough for the dead to cross without brushing the living. He began the toll with a coin and later agreed to accept an image the traveller could bear to lose. People cross more often now because he cannot collect the full fee from anyone who remembers what he first promised.

leaders.name: Iram Stonepause
leaders.angle: A mason lets shades and mortals build the same road on different schedules.
leaders.backstory: Iram inherited a stair that was renewed every forty years by workers who did not live to see it finished. He carved a channel to take each course's weight before the next crew arrived, then invited the shades who had laid the lowest courses to check his work. The stair was finished in his lifetime, and the patches keep his apprentices employed in the next one.

leaders.name: Veda Secondwindow
leaders.angle: One household teaches families to recognize shade kin by familiar routines.
leaders.backstory: Veda kept a room with the blinds open for her brother after he began to fade. He stopped recognizing the street, but his hand always found the window catch he had repaired as a boy. Her dayrooms now leave the things their visitors remember in reach and ask living guests to go home without carrying them away.

leaders.hand_activity: Opens a familiar worn brass window catch

leaders.name: Maris Tallow
leaders.angle: Lighthouse keepers and harbor pilots build maritime authority around safe passage.
leaders.backstory: Maris lost her first ship because two rival captains extinguished a harbor beacon to settle a wager. She bought the ruined tower with her salvage share and persuaded neighboring keepers to answer one another's signals regardless of which flag approached. Their pilots and escort captains now follow her compact of safe passage, giving her a coast to govern and a difficult promise to keep when an enemy asks for rescue.

leaders.name: Orrick
leaders.angle: The Lanun explore and study the changed sea instead of mastering it through piracy or surrendering to it.
leaders.backstory: Orrick inherited an Aifon chart that marked a thriving city where his lead line found only open water. He began paying divers and conjurers to measure the currents, ruins and strange voices that other captains dismissed as bad omens. His survey flotilla follows him for shares in each discovery, although he has started recording dreams that predict soundings he has never taken.

leaders.name: Sella
leaders.angle: Lanun freedom expressed through a fleet of fiercely contractual shareholders and floating markets.
leaders.backstory: Sella won nine shares in a captured vessel by carving its new figurehead from the wreckage of her own boat. Rather than sell them, she divided their profits among shipwrights, cooks and musicians who could make the vessel earn between raids. Her floating markets have grown into a fleet whose crews elect her captain each season, provided the accounts balance and the next voyage promises something worth seeing.

leaders.name: Brannoc Blackwake
leaders.angle: A collective of captains turns the sea's unanswered prayers into an exploitative pact with the Overlords.
leaders.backstory: Brannoc prayed over a becalmed fleet until something beneath it answered in the voices of the drowned. He returned with full holds and taught desperate captains the offerings that would bring the same favor. They now entrust him with their voyages and their prisoners, while he insists that every sailor carried away by the answering tide has merely been promoted to a deeper service.

leaders.name: Ilyra Rope-End
leaders.angle: A privateer coalition makes the Lanun love of freedom apply to captives as well as captains.
leaders.backstory: Ilyra learned rigging while chained aboard a prize ship and escaped by dropping its entire mainsail onto the boarding party that had come to sell her again. The freed rowers chose her to command their stolen vessel, and other escaped crews soon joined it. She finances their war on slave galleys by taking the cargo of any captain who trades in people, a rule that has cost her lucrative allies and earned her fiercely loyal harbor towns.

leaders.name: Dario Reefglass
leaders.angle: A harbor pilots' league takes charge of the shoals the admirals keep sailing through.
leaders.backstory: Dario learned to read silt by looking through the neck of a broken bottle a freebooter left behind. He warned three captains away from the bar the week the harbor lord's own ship went down. The pilots who inherit his bottle earn a berth each year by bringing at least one rival's ship safely home.

leaders.name: Makena Saltstitch
leaders.angle: The caulkers' guild supports free sailors by holding title to the dock that services their ships.
leaders.backstory: Makena scraped the governor's crest off a wreck and built the dock's doors out of its stern. The governor's creditors sued for the doors and found every crew in the harbor had bought a share in them. Warships still dock there, though their captains must wait while the smallest fishing boats come in first.

leaders.name: Carlon Mirrorsail
leaders.angle: A wreckers' chief turns the stranded into labor for his uncharted piers.
leaders.backstory: Carlon survived a wreck on a coast where lights were supposed to show safe water. He spent his compensation on brighter lamps and bribed the surveyors to take his stretch of cliff off their charts. The colony that strips the stranded ships has enough timber for houses and too much rope for most of its workers to leave.

leaders.name: Hessa Sabletide
leaders.angle: A salvager bands divers together against vessels that claim everything on the bottom.
leaders.backstory: Hessa cut loose a divers' bell the admiralty had declared lost while two men were still shut inside it. She entered the salvage award in their names and used her own share to buy communal lines and floats. The crews who train with her are trying to put the same bell to work on a shipwreck the admiralty has refused to admit is there.

leaders.name: Jeron Foghorn
leaders.angle: Crews from rival ports grant safe passage to a weather reader whose forecasts their temples usually suppress.
leaders.backstory: Jeron kept watch for a storm his ship's priest had said would come only if somebody broke a vow. Every ship that followed his forecast instead survived, and the rest of the crews left him their instruments. He moors between hostile ports so that none of them can claim the weather belongs to its god alone.

leaders.name: Hadrin
leaders.angle: The civilian labor that sustains a land of adventurers becomes a source of leadership in its own right.
leaders.backstory: Hadrin followed adventuring companies with a portable oven and learned that every heroic rescue left hungry people behind it. After a dragon burned a frontier town, he rebuilt its mill before anyone could agree whose statue should stand in the square. Settlers and retired adventurers now follow his workshops along the border, where his authority rests on roofs, bread and the stubborn belief that ordinary work deserves its own songs.

leaders.name: Dessa Venn
leaders.angle: Secular culture tests Cassiel's ideas through art, including criticism of Cassiel himself.
leaders.backstory: Dessa fled a royal theater after refusing to rewrite a lost battle as a god's deliberate triumph. In the Grigori cities she found audiences willing to laugh at immortals, then alarmed her patrons by giving Cassiel the least flattering part in her next play. Actors, teachers and disputing societies have made her their speaker, and she defends their right to question even the principles that first gave them refuge.

leaders.name: Ruvik
leaders.angle: A mortal supremacist twists freedom from divine masters into the right of powerful mortals to dominate others.
leaders.backstory: Ruvik became famous for killing a priest's summoned champion and refusing the grateful village's offer of a shrine. He taught his growing band that no god could own a mortal, then declared that a mortal should own whatever strength allowed him to keep. Disaffected adventurers and ambitious frontier captains now acclaim him, while the settlements beneath his protection discover that his contempt for divine tribute does not extend to tribute paid to him.

leaders.name: Nallia Bronzebound
leaders.angle: Grigori independence becomes a practical institution protecting consent against magical coercion.
leaders.backstory: Nallia was a border magistrate when an enchanted witness condemned three innocent refugees. She spent her inheritance learning how to recognize compulsions and training guards who could resist them. Her wardens now administer sanctuary gates for several towns, admitting pilgrims as people while refusing any priest or mage the power to speak another person's consent.

leaders.name: Edren
leaders.angle: An adventurer treats summoning as a mortal craft for hazardous exploration, without priestly patronage.
leaders.backstory: Edren survived two collapsed tombs by sending conjured creatures where a living companion would have died. He returned to the Grigori with treasure, a missing hand and a determination to replace heroic last stands with better preparation. His expedition lodges elect him to direct their ventures, though their increasingly elaborate conjurations raise the question of how much danger can be delegated before courage becomes someone else's burden.

leaders.angle: Print shops give displaced adventurers and minority sects a way to publish their own accounts.
leaders.backstory: Tessa set her first type from lead she scavenged in a shrine the congregation had abandoned. She printed the survivors' account of its burning for less than the price of the priest's official version. The presses that learned from hers have turned the market's broadest street into a place where every lie has to compete for paper.

leaders.angle: Former adventurers use camp courts to settle claims that city judges find inconvenient.
leaders.backstory: Dowen spent a decade dividing salvage between people who came back from the expedition and the families of those who did not. He made a rule about whose turn it was to talk and kept his camp open whenever a judge refused to hear a case. His court handles less patrol pay these days than quarrels over orchards, alleys and absent children.

leaders.angle: A brewers' cartel takes advantage of a popular suspicion of magically treated water.

When it refused, she bought the well rights and stopped telling her customers which water had been treated. Her settlements are prosperous enough to get every child a fresh cup, so long as its parents can keep up with the subscription.

leaders.angle: Librarians keep evidence of their neighbors' religions available in a nation formally estranged from the gods.
leaders.backstory: Gavren inherited six chests of confiscated books and explicit instructions to burn them in public. He burned the chests and moved the contents to any household willing to lend them again. When a magistrate complained that he was running a shrine, he offered to put the complaint in circulation beside the rest of the holdings.

leaders.angle: Independent salvagers insist owners prove they can render dangerous ruins safe before charging for access.
leaders.backstory: Mara found a set of nail marks beside the spells that had made a collapsed tower impassable. She showed her crew how to recognize the safe route and marked every unclaimed chamber they freed. The city's owner sent a revenue guard and discovered someone had nailed his deed to the door of the one room she still refused to open.

leaders.angle: The older Hippus culture of husbandry and sacred obligation offers an alternative to measuring a clan by its contracts.
leaders.backstory: Ulsha inherited the ceremonial herd that her clan had kept through the Age of Ice, including mares too old to ride. When a hungry war captain ordered them slaughtered, she led the herd away and shared its young stock with families whose mounts had been requisitioned. Those families follow her grazing circuit and its rites of thanks, forming a confederacy whose riders owe service to the herd's survival before any employer's purse.

leaders.angle: Hippus speed creates a network of couriers whose political power depends on remaining trustworthy across wars.
leaders.backstory: Hest first earned a captain's pay by carrying a peace offer through three armies that each wanted it to arrive too late. He built a chain of remount stations whose riders swear to deliver a sealed message without asking who profits from it. He pieced those scraps of learning together with riders' weather lore and began shaping harmless dust figures to teach children the old battles. Young riders now gather beneath his painted banners to study a magic that travels with the herd, while traditional captains fear he is rebuilding the very dependence their ancestors escaped.

leaders.angle: Permanent remount towns and the people left behind by campaigning riders become a Hippus political faction.
leaders.backstory: Ereska built stone windbreaks around a winter camp after losing half its foals to a storm while the clan's warriors served abroad. Saddlers, smiths and grazing families stayed to enlarge the camp into a town, then built another where the next remount road ended. She commands their militia and supplies their cousins' companies, insisting that a people can keep its horsemanship without requiring every home to fold into a saddlebag.

leaders.name: Marruk
leaders.angle: The mercenary contract becomes a machinery of perpetual debt and predatory intervention.
leaders.backstory: Marruk discovered that bankrupt cities could still pay a company in pasture rights, hostages and the next season's harvest. He bought the unpaid contracts of other captains and sent their riders to collect, turning one failed campaign into a chain of dependent towns. His creditors' league now offers protection at prices designed never to be repaid, and its riders call every punitive raid the enforcement of an honest bargain.

Stocks of Bekar's bolts are now a better measure of a camp's wealth than the splendor of its tents.

She opened a school above a communal bakery, where apprentices learned to mend roofs and purify water before they were permitted to kindle a battle flame. When the guilds tried to close it, the surrounding wards paid her fines in bread, copper, and sworn service. Her following now treats the blood of Kylorin as a public inheritance whose first duty is to make ordinary lives bearable.

leaders.angle: The magically ungifted people who keep a magical nation working, with authority based on logistics and devices.

leaders.angle: A scholarly necromantic institution that converts regulated research into permanent ownership of its researchers.

Maerith sincerely believes that permitting a brilliant mind to rest while questions remain unanswered is the most wasteful form of murder.

His Quiet Hall shelters dangerous research only when its owners accept that a soldier with no academic rank may order it stopped.

Town militias and disaffected chanters follow her because no locked gate or jealously guarded curriculum has yet kept her music out.

leaders.name: Perpentach, the Gentle Witness
leaders.angle: Perpentach facet: a healer among his inner voices commands a breakaway court that treats his other personalities as usurpers of the same body.
leaders.backstory: When a long-silenced healer among Perpentach's inner voices seized the king's attention, he ordered every carnival slave freed and forbade his court to enter an unwilling mind. At the next feast another voice revoked the decree, but three provincial circuses kept the first command and proclaimed the Gentle Witness their rightful sovereign. They shelter the king whenever his gentler facet prevails and dispatch his own signed letters to recruit soldiers against the courts obeying his other selves. The Witness calls those selves usurpers, even as they answer through his own mouth, and his followers fight to preserve a mercy their king may no longer remember promising.

leaders.name: Perpentach, the Perfect Rehearsal
leaders.angle: Perpentach facet: the Director personality inspires a separatist state of exact cues and bargains, fighting the other royal courts in the name of the same living king.

They claim the Director alone speaks with royal authority and raise armies to bring the king's other courts back to their appointed places. leaders.name: Perpentach, the Empty Audience
leaders.angle: Perpentach facet: the hunger for silence among his inner voices rules a rival puppet court, recruiting living followers and declaring the other facets unfinished roles to be captured.
leaders.backstory: Perpentach discovered that he could briefly quiet an unwanted voice by giving it a summoned puppet and forcing it to perform outside his skull. The personality that savoured that silence founded the Empty Audience, a court of puppets and living courtiers who promise him peace if every troublesome self can be assigned a permanent role. Its ministers obey the king's commands when that facet is ascendant and treat his later pleas to release the captives as interference from the very usurpers they must imprison. Their armies now hunt the Witness's caravans and the Director's stages, while Perpentach can cheer either side because each insists it is rescuing him from the others.

leaders.name: Brassett Nine-Fingers
leaders.angle: The material economy behind the circus: stage machinery, paid crews, and the people required to make arbitrary royal spectacles work.
leaders.backstory: Brassett lost a finger repairing a collapsing royal stage, then charged the treasury for the finger as well as the repair. Ministers laughed until his crews refused to raise the next pavilion and the whole court discovered how much of its magic depended on ropes, pulleys, and unpaid carpenters. He now rules a circuit of carnival towns through contracts that guarantee a wage, a hot meal, and a share of the gate receipts. His workers will build almost any spectacle their patrons can afford, but even a king must pay before the hidden wheels begin to turn.

leaders.name: Velisse the Understudy
leaders.angle: A demon summoned for a stage performance who escapes its binding, appropriates the mimic tradition, and builds an independent rival carnival court.
leaders.backstory: Velisse was a minor demon repeatedly summoned to impersonate absent stars in a royal performance, learning mortal vanity from the applause that greeted each stolen face. During her hundredth curtain call she copied the conjurer's signature onto her own release and walked out of the binding circle in the costume of its tragic queen. Her escaped performers and mimics now enter border towns in the uniforms of their expected defenders, then announce the arrival of an entirely new court. Velisse offers every captive a starring role in her expanding carnival, but keeps their true names and memories as payment so that no one else can ever cast them again.

leaders.name: Ossren Nightferry
leaders.angle: A mercantile Svartalfar river culture connecting secret woodland settlements to the wider world.
leaders.backstory: Ossren inherited a ferry whose passengers were forbidden to admit where they had boarded it. He widened the boat, fitted its oars with leather sleeves, and began bringing medicine and foreign tools upriver between the patrols of both elven courts. His night quays have become meeting places for smugglers, artisans and messengers who would never share a public marketplace. He sells passage to almost anyone but will sink a customer who brings a royal census or an assassin's unpaid debt aboard his boats.

leaders.name: Mirel Widowfern
leaders.angle: A dark elf establishes safe-conduct for people who abandon disputes before killing completes them.
leaders.backstory: Mirel carried a ransom to a council that had already voted to kill her brother. She left the payment on the floor and brought home its youngest guard, who had opened the cellar when nobody else would. Her safe houses fly the guard's badge in reverse and offer the same deal to anybody willing to turn a key.

leaders.name: Sovar Whisperleaf
leaders.angle: Rumor brokers create a market that pays less for lies and more for useful warnings.
leaders.backstory: Sovar was paid for a rumor so good his customer tried to have him killed to stop it being sold twice. He moved into an abandoned theater and fixed a fee for each warning, deducted if the customer could prove it false. The best seats are reserved for the people who correct him in public, which keeps his oldest customers away.

leaders.angle: A ritualist traps dissent in a court where any contradiction becomes testimony against its speaker.
leaders.backstory: Ithra bred a vine that remembered the sound of its keeper's last command. She grew it about a deserted judgment seat and announced that it could hear evidence the living had learned to forget. Speakers now agree with the vine while it is still rustling, in the hope of keeping what they meant to say out of reach.

leaders.angle: A night gardener grows useful passageways through woods that hostile houses still claim to own.
leaders.backstory: Nessar planted the winter gardens of houses that were fighting about whose road could reach the wells. He put his newest cuttings where nobody expected to walk and pruned them until two kitchens found themselves joined by a path. The servants use it in the dark, and their employers have learned to buy herbs from the same old man.

leaders.name: Valira Thinveil
leaders.angle: A disguise artist gives escaped servants names that survive close inquiry.
leaders.backstory: Valira dressed a runner in an expensive disguise that came apart at the first dawn gate. She began again with cheap wool, the accent of her sister's village, and a handful of genuine neighbors willing to vouch. The people she helps remember the invented childhoods less clearly than the real neighbor who arrived first to defend them.

leaders.name: Nemara Vey
leaders.angle: A vampire who accepts eventual death rather than continuing to consume souls; the Calabim's immortality becomes a moral deadline.
leaders.backstory: Nemara heard the last words of a household servant whose soul she had meant to consume, and found herself remembering every other voice she had silenced. She swore never to feast again, knowing that blood alone could not purchase the stolen years on which a Calabim vampire depends. Her estate has become a refuge guarded by mortal soldiers and a few immortals willing to spend their remaining strength without replenishing it. She is training a human successor while rival broods gather at the borders, determined that her last inheritance will be a people who can survive her.

leaders.name: Odran Kessel
leaders.angle: A mortal Calabim administration that survives by preserving the fiction of an absent vampire lord.
leaders.backstory: When his vampire master vanished during a border war, Odran continued issuing the estate's orders behind the closed doors of the audience chamber. The neighbours obeyed because the taxes arrived, the watch remained paid, and nobody wished to be the first to discover that the lord was merely sleeping. Odran has used that uncertainty to suspend the household's feeding levies and arm the villages, while keeping the prisons and informers that make the old authority convincing. His coalition of clerks and militia captains rules in the name of an empty chair whose secret might undo everything it has preserved.

leaders.name: Valesca Dorn
leaders.angle: Vampiric public health and infrastructure pursued as the efficient cultivation of a captive food supply.
leaders.backstory: Valesca considered the grand broods' starving villages a disgraceful waste of the people they intended to devour. She repaired wells, ordered clean granaries and established nurseries, then demonstrated that a healthier estate could surrender more victims without emptying its fields. Dispossessed vampires now finance her model towns, where every kindness is entered beside a projected feeding yield. She intends to cover Calabim territory with prosperous settlements whose inhabitants will never be allowed to mistake good husbandry for freedom.

leaders.name: Istren Vale
leaders.angle: A seductive contractual version of Calabim predation that exports the broods' power through debt instead of annexation.
leaders.backstory: Istren discovered that a foreign merchant would recoil from a slave auction yet willingly sign a contract pledging everything he owned. His counting houses now purchase unpaid obligations abroad and offer debtors comfortable homes inside Calabim borders in exchange for service to a brood. The fine script reserves the right to choose which household member will be surrendered at the final reckoning, and Istren never explains what a vampire takes beyond blood. He dreams of making every neighbouring kingdom dependent on his credit before its rulers notice that their subjects have become his harvest.

leaders.name: Raska Morcant
leaders.angle: A mortal revolutionary who opposes hereditary vampire privilege because she wants predation opened to everyone willing to rise by it.
leaders.backstory: Raska was a bloodpet captain denied the Dark Gift after three decades of keeping her master's villages obedient. She stole a brood register and used its concealed family scandals to persuade a junior vampire to sponsor her rebellion. Her followers demand an end to hereditary privilege, promising that any soldier may earn immortality by delivering enough conquered subjects to the new fraternity. Raska has not yet received the Gift herself, but each victory makes it harder for her patron to deny her without also threatening the hungry army she has built.

leaders.name: Vesna Quayward
leaders.angle: Mortal merchants buy a guarded right of passage for households leaving the feasting estates.
leaders.backstory: Vesna never owned land, which helped the customs officers overlook her first dozen cargoes of people. She paid a new wharf guard every month until the guard and the dockhands asked her to buy their entire company. The company publishes its tariff in the markets and charges less for a person whose master is likely to come looking.

leaders.backstory: Malrec inherited a dye works whose masters were still signing orders long after he went below to rest. He began buying their experiments on the condition that the other lords could see their account books. Now the weavers elect their own night foreman, and the worst part of challenging him is finding a color he has not already bought.

She bought back the right to each of the meals once served on it and spent a decade demonstrating that the meals were worth more than the land. The silver now goes round her table at every auction while stewards outside count the villagers each bid will cost.

He reopened it and set one household to watch its door while he asked the others to leave what they could inside. The lord's reeve says the deficit is all due to rats, and nobody in the family has been unkind enough to contradict him.

leaders.backstory: Dianthe could never prove whether a fellow elder had glamoured her bailiff or merely bribed him. She made a courtroom where the bailiff need only open a shutter to halt proceedings and put his account on the record. The bailiff sits a little more comfortably than was once customary, which may have as much to do with his honesty as the shutters.

leaders.angle: A Sheaim scholar who treats contact with other worlds as a research program rather than a promise of Armageddon.
leaders.backstory: Serev entered a planar gate expecting the paradise his tutor had promised and returned with a map of seventeen incompatible skies. He now leads an itinerant college that records what each gate admits, what it consumes, and which promises its inhabitants break. His followers remain dangerous experimenters, but they oppose the final ritual because destroying creation would destroy their only reliable point of reference. Tebryn calls their caution cowardice; Serev calls it the difference between a discovery and a disappearance.

leaders.angle: An explicitly dissident Sheaim faction uses its knowledge of destructive magic to document its victims and stop the next ritual.

Her faction has not escaped the Sheaim's dangerous magical inheritance, and its claim to goodness rests on accepting that danger themselves instead of charging it to strangers.

leaders.angle: A commercial apocalypse faction whose patrons profit from preparing for the world's end and therefore keep postponing it.

He now finances gatehouses, pyres, and evacuation barges through contracts payable when the final day arrives. He wants creation frightened, indebted, and permanently on the brink, a kingdom of recurring emergencies more profitable than either peace or oblivion.

leaders.angle: Apocalypse as liturgy and collective authorship, distinct from Tebryn's terror and Os-Gabella's private escape.
leaders.backstory: Sethrien once composed funeral hymns for immigrants whose families could not afford a pyre. After hearing a gate answer one of his laments, he founded a congregation that believes every life is a dissonant fragment waiting for creation's final chord. His choirs offer the lonely a place in that supposed masterpiece, then teach them that anyone who refuses to join may be silenced for the harmony of the whole. He seeks neither survival nor reward after Armageddon, only the authority to decide how everyone else's story ends.

leaders.angle: The practical society around planar gates: a fortress district governed by containment specialists rather than prophets.

The other survivors elected the former mechanic their warden after the appointed magisters fled, and their shuttered quarter became a refuge for workers too useful to be allowed to leave. Nesk trades repair work and captured arcane machinery for food, closing breaches without asking whether the creature on either side deserves salvation. He will shelter fugitives who obey his locks, but he will also seal a populated passage if that is the price of keeping the rest of the district intact.

She broke one open, recovered a seed and planted all the ones that sprouted blue in a new row. The fruit keeps a hungry village alive, although every grower takes a turn deciding whether the next batch can be trusted.

leaders.name: Rhuvek Tithekeeper
leaders.angle: An Infernal city built around ownership and predictable extraction instead of Hyborem's impatient violence.
leaders.backstory: Rhuvek was a collector in Mammon's hell before following the first breach into Erebus, where he discovered that demons destroyed valuable subjects faster than they could replace them. He offers conquered settlements protection from casual slaughter in exchange for perpetual obligations that encompass their dead as well as their living. His officers inventory manes as carefully as other rulers count grain, and enforce the distinction between a tenant and an unclaimed victim.
